A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSGD convergence study. The main text, equations, figures and Appendices A–K are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Appendix G reports original simulations on synthetic quadratic objectives, measuring mean-squared error, empirical tail probabilities and network-size effects in Figures 1–2.

after.justification: Appendix G retains these original simulations and Figures 1–2. Their retention from v2 does not alter their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equation (3) retain the same adapt-then-combine DSGD update. The shortened explanation of local updating and consensus does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic quadratic problems on Erdős–Rényi networks, including the 30-user experiment and networks with 25, 50 and 100 users. No additional dataset or test scenario appears.

E2.justification: Appendix G evaluates DSGD under different network sizes in both versions. No competing algorithm is added to or removed from the experiments.

E3.justification: The experiments retain dimension 50, zero initialization, step size 1/(t+1), iteration budgets of 10000 and 3000, and the same MSE and empirical-tail metrics. Network and heterogeneity controls are unchanged.

E4.justification: The same exponential-tail and linear-speed-up analyses remain, including comparisons controlling connectivity and heterogeneity. No new ablation, robustness test or case study is reported.

E5.justification: Appendix G retains 5000 and 1000 runs, respectively, with 3000 and 600 Monte Carlo samples for estimating tail probabilities. Statistical reporting and the plotted uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: All six plot panels in Figures 1–2 are identical across versions, and their reported findings remain unchanged. These include tail decay beginning around iteration 6000 for threshold 10^-4 and faster decay with larger networks.

T1.justification: Appendix B's Proposition 6 corrects the product denominator from t+t0 to k+t0, matching its index k. Section 4 also removes the per-user inequality printed in v2; the averaged inequality remains in Appendix F. The main convergence guarantees are retained.

C1.justification: The relaxed-assumption, optimal-rate and linear-speed-up claims remain. The additional abstract emphasis on transient times, novelty and experiments reiterates claims and evidence already present elsewhere in v2.

C2.justification: The conclusion broadens proposed future extensions from gradient tracking and sub-Weibull noise to bias-correction mechanisms including exact diffusion and heavy-tailed noise. These are future directions; existing interpretations and applicability limitations otherwise remain.

D1.justification: Section 2 removes the explicit optional weighted empirical-risk and nonuniform-sampling explanation from v2's footnote. Experimental implementation details remain unchanged; the added Metropolis–Hastings wording in the speed-up paragraph repeats information already given in the general methodology.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds compact-domain qualifications for prior mirror-descent studies and distinguishes convex from nonconvex settings among clipped methods. The cited works remain the same; reference 45's publication update and the interchange of references 61–62 do not introduce new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, literature review, method description and conclusion are tightened while retaining the narrative structure. Section 4 summarizes an existing Appendix I argument and adds specific appendix pointers. Appendix theorem restatements acquire inconsistent labels 3.4 and 3.7 instead of 1 and 2.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 is relocated, several equations are compacted, and Figure 1 no longer interrupts the linear-speed-up paragraph. The two figures retain identical panels, axes, legends and captions.

improvement.justification: The clearer main-text explanation of Lemma 5's role, explicit pointers to existing experiments and appendices, and corrected Proposition 6 improve readability and precision. These modest benefits outweigh the new appendix-label inconsistencies. The central guarantees and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
